title: Power series over a field or a Cohen ring: complete regular local domain
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be either a field $k$, or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]: a discrete valuation ring (a local principal ideal domain which is not a field) which is complete with respect to its maximal ideal and whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime number $p$ (Algebra, Definition 0327); write $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ for the maximal ideal of $\Lambda$ ($0$ resp. $p\Lambda$). Let $d\ge0$ and $R_0=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then: (1) $R_0$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local integral domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_\Lambda R_0+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_0=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $\mathfrak m_0=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring; (2) the composite $\Lambda\to R_0\to R_0/\mathfrak m_0$ induces an isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R_0/\mathfrak m_0$; (3) $R_0$ is $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; (4) $R_0$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] $d$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $d+1$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring.

source.place: Algebra, Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), first two sentences (stated there without proof); Cohen ring: Definition Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring, line 44872)

proof.text: (The base ring.) In both cases $\Lambda$ is a Noetherian local integral domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$. If $\Lambda=k$ is a field, its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], local with $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=0$, and a domain. If $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], it is a principal ideal domain, so every ideal is finitely generated (by one element) and $\Lambda$ is Noetherian; it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=p\Lambda$, and $p\ne0$ in $\Lambda$ since $\Lambda$ is not a field (its maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ is not $0$).

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: ($R_0$ is a Noetherian domain.) By step 1, $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, so $R_0=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian]; $\Lambda$ is a domain, so $R_0$ is an integral domain [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain].

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: ($R_0$ is local; its maximal ideal.) By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] (b), $R_0$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0=\{F\in R_0: F(0)\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda\}$, $F(0)$ the constant coefficient. We show $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_\Lambda R_0+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. '$\supseteq$': an element $\sum_j\lambda_jG_j+\sum_iX_iH_i$ with $\lambda_j\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ has constant coefficient $\sum_j\lambda_jG_j(0)\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, since $F\mapsto F(0)$ is a ring homomorphism with $X_i(0)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] ($i=d$). '$\subseteq$': for $F\in\mathfrak m_0$, $F=F(0)+(F-F(0))$ with $F(0)\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda\subseteq\mathfrak m_\Lambda R_0$, and $F-F(0)$ has constant coefficient $0$, so lies in the kernel $(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ of $F\mapsto F(0)$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] ($i=d$). Hence $\mathfrak m_0=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda=k$ ($\mathfrak m_\Lambda=0$) and $\mathfrak m_0=pR_0+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring. With step 2 this is clause (1).

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: (Clause (2): the residue field.) Let $\rho:\Lambda\to R_0/\mathfrak m_0$ be the composite $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\bmod\mathfrak m_0$. It is surjective: for $F\in R_0$, $F-F(0)\in(X_1,\ldots,X_d)\subseteq\mathfrak m_0$ (step 3), so $F\equiv F(0)=\rho(F(0))$. Its kernel is $\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\lambda\in\mathfrak m_0\}=\{\lambda:\lambda(0)=\lambda\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda\}=\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ by the description $\mathfrak m_0=\{F:F(0)\in\mathfrak m_\Lambda\}$ of step 3 (the constant coefficient of the constant series $\lambda$ is $\lambda$). Hence $\rho$ induces an isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R_0/\mathfrak m_0$.

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: (Clause (3): completeness.) If $\Lambda=k$, then $\mathfrak m_0=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ (step 3) and $R_0$ is $(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete]. If $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring, then $\Lambda$ is Noetherian (step 1) and $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], and $\mathfrak m_0=pR_0+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ (step 3); so [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] with $J=p\Lambda$ shows that $R_0$ is $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: (Upper bound for the dimension.) Put $n=d$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $n=d+1$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring. By step 3 the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of the Noetherian local ring $R_0$ (step 2) is generated by the $n$ elements $X_1,\ldots,X_d$, resp. $p,X_1,\ldots,X_d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators], $\dim R_0\le n$ (Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]).

Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), stated without proof; proof written by an agent

proof.text: (Clause (4): regularity.) By steps 6 and 7, $\dim R_0=n$, i.e. $d$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $d+1$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring. $R_0$ is a Noetherian local ring (steps 2, 3) whose maximal ideal is generated by $n=\dim R_0$ elements (step 6), so it is a regular local ring by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme].
